title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that compares a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks using a deterministic validator. Under the frozen confirmatory semantics (shared_initial_candidate per pair) all confirmatory episodes completed with baseline = 120/120 verifier passes and guarded (gpt‑5‑mini) = 120/120 verifier passes (paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729; exact McNemar p = 1.0). We (i) publish the exact execution and analysis artifacts and SHA‑256 fingerprints required for byte‑for‑byte reproduction, (ii) show—using archived validator traces and shared‑candidate artifacts—why the preregistered shared‑candidate semantics yields a degenerate paired outcome that does not probe independent generative reliability, and (iii) provide artifact‑grounded, runnable protocol modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory design, validator diversification, and expanded task heterogeneity) that preserve reproducibility while enabling informative independent comparisons.

sections.introduction:
Automating NetOps by translating high‑level operator intent into device configuration commands can reduce human error but demands strong correctness guarantees: reachability, ACL/segmentation invariants, and transient safety during multi‑step changes. Deterministic validators (Batfish‑class analyzers) provide an objective semantic oracle for configuration artifacts and are widely used in pre‑deployment validation [https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]. We preregistered a focused confirmatory experiment to ask: does a single‑pass LLM generation pipeline produce verifier‑valid configurations less often than a deterministic template baseline on a reproducible corpus of operationally constrained intent→configuration tasks? The preregistered estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline over N = 120 programmatic tasks (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663c...).

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment with exhaustive per‑file SHA‑256 manifests enabling byte‑for‑byte reproduction of generation, provider traces, and deterministic validation. (2) Confirmatory quantitative result: under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both baseline and guarded conditions passed the validator on all confirmatory episodes (120/120 each), producing a degenerate paired contrast (estimate 0.00, CI [0.00,0.00], McNemar p = 1.0). (3) An explicit, artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why that outcome is substantively uninformative about independent generative reliability and a precise, runnable set of artifact‑anchored protocol modifications to produce informative inference while preserving reproducibility.
sections.related_work:
Verifier‑grounded NetOps research emphasizes pre‑deployment semantic checking to reduce operational risk; Batfish and related tools document how semantic analysis scales to real networks and materially improves safety [Batfish lessons; https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Prior LLM→NetOps studies examine intent translation, intent→configuration synthesis, and generate–validate–repair loops; they repeatedly highlight that surface fluency metrics fail to capture operational correctness and that verifier grounding is required for safety claims (representative examples: Automation of Network Configuration Generation using LLMs; Intent‑Based Network Configuration Using LLMs [https://doi.org/10.23919/cnsm62983.2024.10814407, https://doi.org/10.1002/nem.70029]).

Positioning. Unlike prior informal or post‑hoc artifact releases, our work preregisters the confirmatory estimand, freezing generation semantics, validator, seeds, and retry policy (see execution/execution_manifest.json). This permits a precise audit of what the confirmatory test actually measured and shows how preregistered choices (here, shared_initial_candidate) determine inferential scope.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and artifacts. The full preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3...) and the exhaustive execution manifest are archived in the submission bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json). The immutable initial master prompt that governed autonomous operations is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The declared model configuration used for the run is recorded in execution/model_configuration.json (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini; SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820).

Task corpus and templating. Tasks (N = 120) were programmatically synthesized from a deterministic template bank (generator_id deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, version 5.0). Tasks are balanced across three topology classes per preregistration (edge, datacenter, multi‑AS; 40 tasks each) and include an explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, and workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups). Representative task manifests and seeds are published under execution/task_manifest.jsonl; example task entries and their reference answers are available in the artifact_examples section (e.g., task‑000001 reference and response files).

Generation semantics and adapter. The confirmatory run used preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate": one canonical candidate per pair (seed_0) was generated and presented identically to both baseline and guarded scoring episodes to isolate scoring behavior. The hosted adapter family used was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (provider traces archived under execution/provider_calls/*.json). Because the shared candidate was used for both conditions, the run recorded 120 model generations for 120 pairs (model_calls_used = 120) and completed all planned episodes (planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240). All raw candidate strings are archived (execution/responses/*‑shared‑initial.txt; representative SHA‑256: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...).

Deterministic validator and scoring protocol. Candidate configurations were scored with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0) using the scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation. The validator (1) parses commands and normalizes sequences, (2) enforces task workflow_policies and transient safety invariants, (3) computes final_state reachability and ACL constraints, and (4) emits a detailed JSON trace per episode (execution/scoring/*.json; representative file execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...). The validator output includes parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, final_state, and violation_count (0 for pass). Scoring JSONs and validator traces are archived for every episode so readers can inspect exact failure diagnostics where present.
sections.results:
Confirmatory quantitative outcome. All preregistered confirmatory episodes completed without infrastructure failures (complete_pair_count = 120). The aggregated confirmatory counts are: baseline_success_count = 120/120 (success rate = 1.00) and guarded_success_count = 120/120 (success rate = 1.00). The paired contingency table is degenerate: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c7e...). The paired estimator (mean of guarded_i − baseline_i) = 0.00. The preregistered inferential procedures produced a degenerate 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0.

Representative episode diagnostics. Archived per‑episode scoring JSONs provide exact validator traces. Example: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...) contains before/after final_state, normalized candidate, parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, and violation_count = 0. The identical canonical candidate for pair‑000001 appears in execution/responses/task-000001‑shared‑initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8be...). Multiple pairs show identical SHA‑256 fingerprints across baseline/guarded/shared responses (see execution/execution_manifest.json), documenting that identical artifacts were evaluated in both conditions.

Contamination and missingness. Preregistered contamination heuristics (exact match and normalized n‑gram overlap) flagged no confirmatory candidates under the chosen thresholds; their results are recorded in analysis/contamination_summary.csv. Missingness handling followed the preregistered policy: no infrastructure failures occurred, so no pairs were excluded (missingness_summary shows complete_pairs = 120). All provider call traces and call_cache artifacts are published to permit stronger independent exposure analyses (execution/call_cache/*.json).
sections.discussion:
Why the confirmatory result is uninformative about independent generative reliability. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally removed independent generation variability by generating a single canonical candidate per pair and scoring that identical artifact under both conditions. This design isolates scoring differences but, when a deterministic validator enforces task‑aligned constraints and the shared candidate satisfies them, the paired contrast is necessarily degenerate (both conditions receive the same judgement). The archived artifacts (execution/responses/*‑shared‑initial.txt and execution/scoring/*.json) document this identicality and thus explain the observed 120/120 = 120/120 outcome.

Operational interpretation. For deployment decisions the operational question is typically the LLM's independent per‑condition probability of producing a verifier‑valid candidate (i.e., the generative reliability under stochastic sampling). The current confirmatory test does not estimate that quantity. Artifact‑grounded remediation is straightforward and reproducible: reexecute the scoring harness with independent_per_condition sampling (one independently drawn candidate per condition per pair) or with K distinct seeds per condition (multi‑seed confirmatory). All code, seeds, and the validator are archived so these reruns are deterministic and auditable (see execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/model_configuration.json). The run artifacts therefore support immediate, exact reruns that answer the independent sampling question without introducing new data.

Protocol recommendations for informative verifier‑grounded inference. (1) Confirmatory independent_per_condition: keep paired design but generate independent candidates per condition and use the same paired analysis on per‑task best‑of‑K or per‑seed results. (2) Multi‑seed confirmatory: predefine K ≥ 3 seeds per condition and use bootstrapped inference on per‑condition pass probabilities. (3) Validator diversification: include a second independent verifier (e.g., reachability/emulation) and report intersected pass rates to reduce validator–task coupling. All three modifications are implementable using the published harness and manifest.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and published a complete artifact bundle enabling exact reproduction (execution/execution_manifest.json). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both the deterministic template baseline and the declared gpt‑5‑mini guarded pipeline validated on all confirmatory episodes (120/120 each). Archived artifacts show that identical canonical candidates per pair and template‑aligned tasks caused the degenerate paired result; hence, the confirmatory outcome is arithmetically correct but substantively uninformative about independent LLM generative reliability. We provide artifact‑anchored, runnable protocol modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory execution, validator diversification, task heterogeneity expansion) that preserve determinism and permit informative independent comparisons. All execution and analysis artifacts—including the immutable master prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and the preregistration SHA‑256—are included in the submission bundle to permit exact audit and follow‑up experiments. Transparent preregistration plus exhaustive artifact publication clarifies the precise target of any confirmatory test and accelerates corrective reruns that answer the operational questions NetOps practitioners need for deployment decisions.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
